skill.name: alphafold-database
skill.description: Retrieve AlphaFold protein predictions, download structure files, assess pLDDT and PAE confidence, and plan structural biology workflows.
skill.summary: Access and evaluate AlphaFold DB protein structure predictions.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation syntax, public scientific endpoints, or expected structure downloads. Two examples are confirmed: an unverified pipe-to-shell installer and shell-based command construction with injectable parameters. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The Google Cloud SDK example downloads a remote script and pipes it directly to Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a package-manager installation or a pinned installer whose checksum is verified before execution.

remediation.issue: The proteome download example builds a shell command from function parameters and runs it with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Pass gsutil and its arguments as a list, validate taxonomy IDs, and restrict output paths to an approved directory.

content.value_statement: Finding and interpreting predicted protein structures requires several APIs, formats, and confidence measures. This skill organizes AlphaFold DB retrieval, downloads, confidence analysis, and bulk workflows.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve AlphaFold prediction metadata by UniProt accession.
Download predicted structures in mmCIF, binary CIF, or PDB formats.
Retrieve and interpret per-residue pLDDT scores and PAE matrices.
Parse structures and extract coordinates or confidence values with Biopython.
Plan batch retrieval with Google Cloud Storage and BigQuery.
Compare confidence summaries across multiple protein predictions.
limitations: AlphaFold predictions are computational models, not experimental structures.
Most retrieval workflows require internet access and third-party scientific services.
Predictions may omit ligands, cofactors, modifications, and multichain interactions.
The reference includes unsafe installation and shell-command examples that require remediation before execution.

use_cases.title: Assess a Research Target
use_cases.description: Retrieve one protein prediction and identify regions suitable for structural interpretation using pLDDT and PAE.

use_cases.title: Prepare Docking Inputs
use_cases.description: Download a target structure and document confidence limits before selecting regions for docking studies.

use_cases.title: Screen a Protein Set
use_cases.description: Build a batch workflow that summarizes prediction coverage and high-confidence residue fractions across many accessions.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Prediction
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the AlphaFold DB prediction for UniProt accession {accession}. Summarize the entry, available files, model version, and basic confidence information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner retrieval for one known protein

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Confidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze pLDDT and PAE for {accession}. Identify reliable regions, uncertain regions, and domain relationships. Explain limits for {intended_use}.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Protein Predictions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare AlphaFold predictions for {accession_list}. Report coverage, average pLDDT, high-confidence fractions, and major PAE differences using consistent criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Bulk Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible workflow for {species_or_dataset}. Use AlphaFold cloud data, version tracking, caching, validation, rate limits, and confidence summaries.

output_examples.input: Retrieve AlphaFold information for UniProt P00520.
output_examples.output: The result identifies the matching AlphaFold entry, available coordinate files, confidence resources, sequence coverage, and the reported database version.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a low-confidence tail is suitable for detailed modeling.
output_examples.output: The tail has limited local structural reliability. Treat its conformation as uncertain and avoid detailed mechanistic conclusions without supporting experimental evidence.

output_examples.input: Plan a comparison of three protein predictions.
output: Use the same AlphaFold database version for every accession.
Compare sequence coverage, mean pLDDT, high-confidence fractions, and PAE domain patterns.
Record missing entries and retrieval errors separately from low-confidence predictions.

best_practices: Check pLDDT and PAE before using a predicted structure for downstream analysis.
Record accession, fragment, and database version with every downloaded file.
Use caching, timeouts, status checks, and rate limits for repeatable retrieval.
anti_patterns: Do not treat predicted coordinates as experimentally validated structures.
Do not infer reliable domain arrangements from pLDDT alone.
Do not execute remote installers or parameterized shell commands without verification and input validation.

faq.question: What identifier should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a UniProt accession when possible. AlphaFold entry identifiers can also identify a specific fragment.

faq.question: Which structure format should I use?
faq.answer: Use mmCIF for modern structural workflows. Use PDB only when a compatible legacy tool requires it.

faq.question: What does pLDDT measure?
faq.answer: pLDDT estimates local confidence for each residue. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in the local predicted geometry.

faq.question: What does PAE measure?
faq.answer: PAE estimates uncertainty in the relative positions of residue pairs. It is especially useful for assessing domain arrangements.

faq.question: Can this skill validate a drug target?
faq.answer: No. It can support structural assessment, but target validation requires biological, experimental, and clinical evidence.

faq.question: Does the skill require network access?
faq.answer: Yes for retrieval and cloud workflows. Analysis of previously downloaded structure and confidence files can run locally.
